title: The Fixed Opener
purpose: Beats 2 and 3 of the 60-second cold open. Recorded once, reused on every episode in the series. Only beat 1 (the problem) changes per zone. Beat 3 ends with the zone name and session length dropped in, which is the one line re-recorded or captioned per episode.

beats.label: What 6S is
beats.vo: 6S is six steps, always in the same order. Sort, keep what earns its place and route out the rest. Straighten, give what stays a home you can reach. Shine, clean closely enough to catch the small problems early. Safety, the fourth step, make the space safe before you make it pretty. Standardize, set the state you want so anyone can find it again. And Sustain, keep it with a habit rather than a burst of willpower.

shots.action: Six titled cards deal onto the screen in order over warm b-roll of hands working a shelf. Each card carries its S name and a one-word verb. The fourth card, Safety, lands with a brief hold so it reads as the fourth step, not an afterthought.
shots.vo_sync: 6S is six steps, always in the same order.

on_screen_text.when: as the first three cards deal
held briefly on the fourth card
as the last two cards deal

beats.label: The solution, the Micro Zone Room Reset
beats.vo: Most home projects fail because a room is too big to finish in one sitting, so you stop halfway and the mess wins. A micro zone is small enough to finish. One shelf, one drawer, one corner. Six steps, one sitting, and a change you can see from the doorway. That is the 6S Success Home Edition Micro Zone Room Reset. Today we reset the [ZONE NAME], and it takes about [SESSION LENGTH].

shots.action: A cluttered corner sits untouched, then a match-cut to the same corner finished and calm. No hands, just the before and after of one small zone.
shots.vo_sync: A micro zone is small enough to finish.

shots.action: The series wordmark, then the swapped-in zone name and session length for this episode.
shots.vo_sync: Today we reset the [ZONE NAME], and it takes about [SESSION LENGTH].

production_note: Beat 2's six-card graphic and beat 1's structure are the only truly fixed frames. Beat 3 is fixed except for the final sentence, where the zone name and session length are swapped per episode, either as a re-recorded closing line or as a caption over a held title card. Keep the fourth card, Safety, on its short hold in every cut, since this is the series' guard against the five-S mistake that keeps appearing elsewhere in the project.
